description: I'm a Python/Backend dev. Our team is building LumenOS, a Space Mission Design Game simulating orbital thermal trade-offs. Our stack is Python, Streamlit, Plotly. We are focused on physics-based AI scheduling for space missions.
summary:
Traditional Earth-observation satellites face a critical latency bottleneck: they collect gigabytes of crisis imagery but must wait 45 to 90 minutes for a ground station pass before downlink and analysis. During catastrophic wildfires, river floods, volcanic eruptions, and solar storms, this latency delays life-saving interventions.

To solve this, we developed LumenOS, an interactive 3D orbital simulation and mission architecture platform modeling an in-orbit Edge AI Data Center Constellation in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). Powered by authentic aerospace physics verified against NASA GMAT R2022a, LumenOS simulates satellites equipped with 24-TOPS radiation-hardened neural compute blades, Stefan-Boltzmann active thermal radiators, and 1550 nm optical inter-satellite laser links. 

Integrating real-world NASA and space agency data—including NASA FIRMS fire detections, TSIS-1 solar irradiance, CERES radiation fluxes, and DONKI space-weather telemetry—LumenOS enables real-time onboard neural inference (FireNet SWIR, HydroMask SAR) that compresses raw data 50:1 into instantaneous alerts. LumenOS proves how autonomous in-orbit computing can transform planetary disaster response and aerospace education.
details:
Project Details

1. What It Does & How It Works

LumenOS is an interactive 3D orbital simulation game and educational space mission architecture platform. It demonstrates how an interconnected constellation of Orbital AI Data Center Satellites in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) can eliminate the critical 45–90 minute ground-station downlink bottleneck during planetary emergencies.

Instead of storing raw imagery and waiting for a ground station pass, LumenOS models:

  • Onboard Edge AI Inference: 24-TOPS radiation-hardened neural processing units run real-time computer vision models (FireNet SWIR, HydroMask SAR) directly over crisis hotspots.
  • In-Orbit Data Reduction: Compresses multi-spectral imagery up to 50:1 into lightweight GeoJSON perimeter and severity alert vectors.
  • Dynamic Optical Laser Crosslinks (1550 nm ISL Mesh): Instantly beams compressed emergency alerts across an inter-satellite laser mesh to high-orbit flagship mother stations (LUMEN-DC-ALPHA) and emergency response stations in real time.
  • Authentic Aerospace Subsystems: Spacecraft buses feature deployable Stefan-Boltzmann thermal radiator wings with micro-channel heat pipes to dissipate heavy compute heat into deep space, alongside rotary sun-tracking GaAs photovoltaic arrays.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Minutes, Not Hours, for First Responders: Slashes disaster latency from 45–90 minutes down to seconds, providing emergency teams with immediate perimeter data during flash floods, crown wildfires, and volcanic plume dispersion.
  • Democratizing Aerospace Education: Bridges authentic aerospace engineering physics with accessible, high-framerate 3D interactive gameplay. Students, educators, and space enthusiasts can learn orbital mechanics, thermal equilibrium, power duty cycles, and link budgets firsthand.
  • Zero-Barrier Universal Access: Thanks to an autonomous client-side simulation engine, LumenOS operates 100% offline in any modern browser without servers, API keys, or specialized hardware.

3. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & 3D Graphics: TypeScript, React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, and custom GLSL WebGL shaders for atmospheric Rayleigh/Mie scattering, dynamic procedural wildfires, flood water dynamics, volcanic tephra columns, and undulating polar auroral ribbons.
  • Backend Architecture: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, WebSockets (for 4-player cooperative multiplayer room synchronization), and Pydantic v2 data models.
  • NASA Validation & Ephemeris: Validated against NASA’s General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT R2022a) and NORAD Two-Line Element (TLE) satellite ephemeris.
  • Authoritative Data Ingestion: NASA FIRMS (VIIRS 375m active fire detections), NASA TSIS-1 (Total Solar Irradiance), NASA CERES EBAF (TOA Earth albedo and outgoing IR radiation), NASA DONKI & NOAA SWPC (solar flare and CME telemetry), and Copernicus Sentinel-1/5P datasets.
  • Testing & Deployment: Vitest (112 unit/component tests, 100% pass), Pytest (390 backend tests), and automated continuous deployment on Vercel.

4. Creativity & Innovation

LumenOS reimagines spacecraft design around the reality of in-orbit computing. Rather than generic sci-fi ships, our 3D spacecraft CAD hangar and flight deck model the physical constraints of spaceborne AI: massive computational heat rejected through deployable radiator louvers, power balancing across orbital eclipse umbras, and laser link line-of-sight geometry around Earth's limb.

Furthermore, LumenOS provides dual gameplay modalities:

  1. Cadet 3D Flight Deck (/play): A 60 FPS flight simulator featuring 3-axis RCS attitude control, nadir sensor targeting, 3-step action loops ([E] Scan → [R] Edge AI → [F] Optical Beam), and Lumi, an intelligent copilot assistant.
  2. Expert Operations Center (/operate): A 4-station mission control console (Mission Director, Systems Engineer, Science Officer, Flight Controller) with real-time multiplayer WebSocket synchronization and 5-minute forward predictive physics forecasting.

5. Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Scientific Rigor vs. Playability: Ensured physical equations (Keplerian two-body mechanics, J2J_2J2​ secular oblateness drift, lumped-capacitance thermodynamics, Free-Space Path Loss) are authentic while keeping the controls responsive and engaging.
  • Strict Epistemic Barriers: In our predictive advisory engine, forecast models project forward using strictly deterministic orbital physics, with zero cheat leakage of future stochastic disaster events.
  • Scientific Data Transparency: Created a 4-tier semantic provenance taxonomy (REAL_NASA_REFERENCE, SIMULATED_SPACECRAFT, SIMULATED_ENVIRONMENT, MODEL_PREDICTION) so users always know which metrics are empirical NASA data and which are simulated.
  • Universal Accessibility: Built non-color-only UI indicators, full keyboard navigation, screen-reader telemetry tables, and offline fallback datasets so any student on any device can participate.
